entries.In the days before Haldric the First sav: In the days before Haldric the First saved our people and founded the kingdom of Wesnoth, we came from an island kingdom far to the west...
entries.They were the vanquished refugees of som: They were the vanquished refugees of some war, fleeing from their homes in a land even further off into the west. The Wesfolk were not numerous, but they used dark magic, commanding vengeful spirits and legions of walking dead...
entries.After a time of great struggle, a peace: After a time of great struggle, a peace was reached. We came to dominate most of the Isle, with the Wesfolk pushed on to the most marginal of lands. In confronting their vile legions, we grew strong. Indeed it was from this war we gleaned our first shards of knowledge about magic.
entries.Things were worse still when sailing to: Things were worse still when sailing to the east. A strong, cold ocean current swept down from the north in the Eastern Ocean, pushing all ships horribly off course. Ships that travelled east and returned reported nothing but open ocean and vile sea monsters...
Over time our skills as navigators grew. Then, one day, the strong-hearted Crown Prince of Southbay returned home from a long voyage with a fabulous tale. He said that there were lands to the east that could be reached by aggressively sailing to the east and north, to compensate for the southern pull of the ocean.
entries.It wasn’t long after he returned that th: It wasn’t long after he returned that the very Crown Prince who discovered the land to the east fell ill and died under mysterious circumstances. His younger brother, and next in line to the throne, chafed at the eye of suspicion cast upon him. He conspired to start a war of distraction with the poor Wesfolk kingdoms and their Lich-Lords.
entries.We must inquire of the survivors after w: We must enquire of the survivors after we defeat them. Onwards to victory!
entries.They pledged to visit all of the terrors: They pledged to visit all of the terrors of the hells upon the Isle. They built a great stone gate to the heart of the homeland of the orcs in the distant west! Now even us Wesfolk must flee or be slaves.
entries.We must prepare the defenses! Haldric, s: We must prepare the defences! Haldric, stay at the keep. I must go and fortify our frontier.
entries.Summer passes into fall, and King Eldari: Summer passes into autumn, and King Eldaric fortifies his frontiers. It is not long before the first orcish scouts are spotted. War has come to the valley.
entries.Nice? The orcs have come, and we must fl: Nice? The orcs have come and we must flee!
entries.Fool boy! Where did you grow up? Enough: Fool boy! Where did you grow up? Enough of this, let’s get some orcs!
entries.Now, should I go southeast on the river: Now, should I go south-east on the river road, or south-west through the Midlands? The river road crosses the Swamp of Esten, so I doubt that even orcs would go there. The Midlands were nice, but who knows what’s going on there now.
entries.We’ve escaped the pass. Well, at least I: We’ve escaped the pass. Well, at least I know that the orcs can be beaten. Hmm, I suppose that this is the last I’ll see of my home... and my father. (Sigh)
entries.The river road follows the Isle’s greate: The river road follows the Isle’s greatest river to the south-east. This road leads to the Isle’s second largest city, Clearwater Port. It would likely have been the Isle’s largest city save for the events of the Wesfolk War. The Lich-Lords befouled much of the land around the river during the course of a great battle. Now the swamp is home to a Wesfolk-imitating cult.
entries.With great trepidation, Prince Haldric l: With great trepidation, Prince Haldric leads his refugee band into the Swamp of Esten. In the centre of that very swamp a shroud of fog descends over young Prince Haldric.
entries.I have a very bad feeling about this. Th: I have a very bad feeling about this. This awful swamp and its crazy cult... Before these troubles started we used to have to clear the swamp every spring and autumn.
entries.May I live forever in Undeath!: May I live for ever in Undeath!
entries.I’m Haldric; my father was King Eldaric: I’m Haldric; my father was King Eldaric IV in the lands north-west of here. Soldier, have you deserted your post?
entries.Well, we can’t go back, and the road ahe: Well, we can’t go back, and the road ahead is blocked. I suppose we’ll have to risk it and go through the Oldwood forest, then make a break for Clearwater Port.
entries.To the southwest lay the Midlands. These: To the south-west lay the Midlands. These were prosperous kingdoms, nestled between hill and forest. These had been the breadbasket of the Green Isle, exporting lumber and gemstones as well. The Midland kingdoms fed the city of Southbay, the largest city on the Isle. The coming of the orcs threatened to lay waste to all this.
entries.They’re attacking the Chief! Kill the me: They’re attacking the Chief! Kill the meat before it gets any further!
entries.I’m Haldric, my father was King Eldaric: I’m Haldric, my father was King Eldaric IV in the lands north-west of here. Soldier, aren’t you on the wrong side of the lines?
entries.They overran my post. I got hit on the h: They overran my post. I got hit on the head pretty good. When I came to, the orcish army had already passed my position.
entries.Well, we can’t go back, and the road ahe: Well, we can’t go back, and the road ahead is blocked... I suppose we’ll have to risk it and go through the Oldwood forest, then make a break for Clearwater Port.
entries.After we drove your kind off we figured: After we drove your kind off we worked out how to break the spell that holds the Evil in the catacombs, and keeps others from entering them.
entries.The lich was carrying a powerful artifac: The lich was carrying a powerful artefact. We know, we can feel it. This artefact may aid you in your quest.
entries.He must mean the Ruby of Fire. It was ou: He must mean the Ruby of Fire. It was our most powerful artefact. We brought it with us from the Old Continent, long ago. We thought it was lost in the war with your people, when Lich-Lord Lenvan fell!
entries.Haldric, we are an ancient people who li: Haldric, we are an ancient people who lived in a land filled with all manner of man and beast. We needed vision that extended beyond the meagre span of human years. The art of necromancy allowed our best and brightest to live for ever, and our worst got to serve as mindless slaves.
entries.Free! I’m free at last! No mere magi cou: Free! I’m free at last! No mere magi could seal me in here for ever! Rise, my soldiers of darkness, the world will be ours once more!
entries.Prince Haldric has emerged from the Lich: Prince Haldric has emerged from the Lich-Lord’s tomb, with the Ruby of Fire. The forest seems particularly bright this day, but there is a cold breeze. It is late autumn, and the first snows should fall any day. Prince Haldric has returned to his forest keep, and is pondering what to do next...
entries.I have the jewel, but I have no idea wha: I have the jewel, but I have no idea what it does. To make matters worse, I have no idea what’s going on outside this forest. The number of refugees is growing daily. We need to get to Southbay, but I dare not lead us on to the plains and risk a slaughter.
entries.We’re only holding the city until the la: We’re only holding the city until the last of the refugees are gone. You, my lord, are free to retreat to safety when the next ship comes. But, if I may be frank, my lord, our defences are stretched thin and we could use all the help we can get to hold our walls. Otherwise I fear that we will be overrun before the last of the people can be evacuated.
entries.Well, we are the last of the refugees fr: Well, we are the last of the refugees from our lands, for the orcs are right on our heels! We have Wesfolk with us. They have been of service. They are to be evacuated as well. We have travelled far and bear many wounded, but we will help you defend these walls as long as we can.
entries.To your posts, men! We should be able to: To your posts, men! We should be able to evacuate everyone in three more boat loads. Until then, let us make those orcs pay dearly for every inch of our land. For our homes, for our people, for our fallen king!
entries.<i>“Bring these Wesfolk too? It would be: ‘Bring these Wesfolk too? It would be... highly irregular.’ Bah! I’ll show you irregular...
entries.My lord, the ship isn’t here yet. Come h: My lord, the ship isn’t here yet. Come and help us defend against the orcs.
entries.I knew you as a boy, and your people hav: I knew you as a boy, and your people have preceded you. Your father was an honourable man, and so are you. Aren’t you the king now?
entries.First, I <i>can</i> translate the book t: First, I can translate the book that will allow Haldric to use the Ruby of Fire. The artefact should help with what must come.
entries.Some favor your people did for us. Why f: Some favour your people did for us. Why flee at all? And why east? We’ve already repelled one orcish assault. We should be working towards taking back the Isle.
entries.If there is no other way. May the bards: If there is no other way. May the bards for ever sing of the valour of the Kings of Southbay! Jessene, about that book?
entries.I’ll begin my translation. Oh, and you s: I’ll begin my translation. Oh, and you should seal the sewer entrance.
entries.I think I’ve figured something out. Look: I think I’ve worked something out. Look.
entries.Ouch! Hot, hot, hot! Gee, somebody shoul: Ouch! Hot, hot, hot! Gee, somebody should really attach this thing to a sceptre or something! I think I’ll save it for closer-ranged combat for now.
entries.There’s not much we can do about that no: There’s not much we can do about that now. I dub this fine ship the Eldaric, in honour of my father. About that island...
entries.Several days later Prince Haldric depart: Several days later Prince Haldric departs in his ship, the Eldaric, his home and the Green Isle lost to him for ever. Before him lay a vast expanse of stormy seas, and the mysterious island that Lady Jessene has mentioned, and even more exotic lands even further to the East.
entries.This is the Elder Prince’s island all ri: This is the Elder Prince’s island all right. We had a heck of a time pacifying the drakes who live here. Oh my, it looks like they’ve re-armed!
entries.Do I need to say, <i>“I told you so”</i>: Do I need to say, ‘I told you so’?
entries.After a week’s steady sailing eastward,: After a week’s steady sailing eastwards, they begin to hear the cries of gulls and feel the loom of the land. The Great Continent appears before them over the summer-lit seas.
entries.Our lands are become full, and our mines: Our lands are become full, and our mines go to the bottom of the world. We have won our war against those things that live in the dark. By what right do you claim all of the forests of the world, and all of the land south of the Great River, and force us on to only the hills and mountains of the north? There are hills and mountains as good as any here in the south!
entries.Hmph! You namby-pamby elves: <i>“We don’: Hmph! You namby-pamby elves: ‘We don’t cut the trees, we groom the forest.’ Our axes can get the wood for a fifth of the cost! I can charge half of what your people do, and still be rich, and I’m not the first to have the thought!
entries.Gee, and you were practicing that speech: Gee, and you were practising that speech for days. I suppose that’s it for diplomacy, then. Haldric, we should avoid bloodshed even if we have to ward them off. There has to be a peaceful resolution to this.
entries.In the name of... This is the continent: In the name of... This is the continent of my home. But I set out east. I must have travelled clear around the world.
entries.Man the ships with skeleton crews, and g: Man the ships with skeleton crews, and give them the remaining supplies. Pass the word to Lord Typhon. Make sure that no more than a third of the fleet is sent. We must not provide the orcs with a ready-made fleet. Make haste, return before it is time to meet these, what are they? Ahh, elves.
entries.I come bearing news. Some ‘old friends’: I come bearing news. Some ‘old friends’ have decided to make an appearance. You should go and ‘greet’ them.
And he bears an artefact of some power. The orcs would not be able to sense that. There is some hand we cannot see at work here.
entries.We may have decided wrongly. If the huma: We may have decided wrongly. If the humans drive the orcs off we should honour our pledge. If more trouble follows them here we should let them fight it out, then we should ‘deal’ with the survivors, and make a compromise with the dwarves.
entries.—And raise your dead to serve us forever: —And raise your dead to serve us for ever!
entries.Recent events have taught me one thing:: Recent events have taught me one thing: that survival trumps honour. Besides, they won’t be screaming at me — I’ll be dead.
entries.I’ll be dead. I mean we can’t just say t: I’ll be dead. I mean we can’t just say that we gave away the Ruby of Fire, or send Jevyan a letter. Well, we are going to say it — but that’s not the point. Jessene, you will forge a very official looking treaty, in which we give the elves the Ruby of Fire, in return for our place here.
entries.I’m going to face Jevyan, and if rumors: I’m going to face Jevyan, and if rumours of his power are true he’s going to pick that treaty off my mangled corpse. Then, you will destroy Jevyan after word of the treaty has spread to the orcs, but before he has a chance to read my undead mind...
Haldric! I won’t do it... I won’t help. What is wrong with your kind, always rushing to a fool’s death? Who’ll lead these people? I... we need you alive.
entries.You’ve denied me honorable death twice a: You’ve denied me honourable death twice already. Once when you arrived at Clearwater Port, and once again when your ships rescued me. I’ll not be denied in this a third time!
entries.Sir, my family has been slaughtered, and: Sir, my family has been slaughtered, and my home lost. All I long for is to join them. Give me this honourable death... Please, Sir! I beg you!
entries.After this conflict is over I’ll have to: After this conflict is over I’ll have to suffer through the long years alone, with no honourable way of joining them. I want to look that monster Jevyan in the eye before I go! I won’t be denied!
entries.Very well, if you can’t be deterred. Rem: Very well, if you can’t be deterred. Remember, you must be slain by the hand of Jevyan himself. We can’t have an illiterate orc or mindless skeleton getting the treaty. We will honour your sacrifice.
entries.Honor me by destroying Jevyan! Preferabl: Honour me by destroying Jevyan! Preferably before he can do unnatural things to me. I want to rest in the ground, not be some mindless undead slave for all eternity!
entries.We’ll have to be careful to let one of t: We’ll have to be careful to let one of the orcish leaders escape back to the Green Isle with the knowledge that the elves ‘have’ the Ruby of Fire. Sheesh... What is your kind’s infatuation with rushing to an ‘honourable death’?
entries.No! I don’t believe it. Only a fool woul: No! I don’t believe it. Only a fool would give away an artefact of such power.
entries.We don’t need some magic trinket to beat: We don’t need some magic trinket to beat you! Prepare to meet your fate, you decrepit sack of bones! For the honour of all of the people of the west-north!
entries.You deny me my honorable death? Our foes: You deny me my honourable death? Our foes are not yet convinced that the elves have the ruby.
entries.We’ll see about that. For the honor of C: We’ll see about that. For the honour of Commander Aethyr, forwards!
entries.After that, we should build towns in all: After that we should build towns in all of the regions that the elves have given us. We should move our capital inland, away from the coast. I hope the children of the good people of the west-north, of the Green Isle, find prosperity in this new land.
entries.The word ‘Wesfolk’ is from your old tong: The word ‘Wesfolk’ is from your old tongue. It means ‘People of the West’. The elves call us the people of the west-north. Under the same old tongue that would be ‘Wes Noth’. So I suggest that the new kingdom be called ‘Wesnoth’, in honour of our old home.
entries.There are many Wesfolk amongst the remai: There are many Wesfolk amongst the remains of my people. We must stay united under one banner. I will need you by my side if there is any hope of building a true ‘Kingdom of Wesnoth’. I... I think a Queen’s crown would sit well upon that flame-coloured hair of yours, Jessene.
entries.Today he is a young man, by his devotion: Today he is a young man, but by his devotion to the crown he is seeking to become a Lord — to join the elite of humanity.
entries.Cold and beautiful, she maintains her et: Cold and beautiful, she maintains her eternal youthful appearance by drinking the blood of the living.
entries.As the leaders of the human Kingdoms, Ki: As the leaders of the human kingdoms, Kings are responsible for ruling and protecting their subjects. Kings can co-ordinate the attacks of level 1 and 2 units, thereby increasing their fighting efficiency.
entries.Born in the Wesfolk aristocracy, she and: Born in the Wesfolk aristocracy, she and her people were excluded from society by their lords, who betrayed their loyalty when a war against Haldric’s people was being lost. This outcast still conserves her nobleness in her veins, and on the battlefield she has earned valuable experience, which she can lend to her people for turning a fight in their favour.
entries.Well, at least we don’t have to contend: Well, at least we don’t have to contend with the undead. No offence, Jessene.
entries.You were planning on sharing this with m: You were planning on sharing this with me, when?
